newsitem.title: USA: A chronology of events in 30-month Espy probe.
newsitem.headline: A chronology of events in 30-month Espy probe.

text.p: A chronology of major events related to the investigation of former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy:

-- Aug. 9, 1994 - Attorney General Janet Reno asks for independent counsel to investigate Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy for allegedly accepting gifts that included Super Bowl tickets, a scholarship for his girlfriend and a leased Jeep Cherokee in violation of federal ethics laws.
-- May 22, 1996 - Federal grand jury charges Mississippi farmer Brook Keith Mitchell with improperly collecting crop subsidies by conspiring with Espy's former chief of staff.

-- July 9, 1996 - Federal grand jury in New Orleans indicts Henry Espy, brother of former the Agriculture Department secretary, for bank fraud and money laundering. Indictment alleged that Henry Espy lied to a bank to cover up the source of illegal campaign contributions.
-- June 13, 1996 - Federal grand jury indicts Sun Diamond Growers of California for giving illegal gifts to Espy.
-- Sept. 17, 1996 - Federal grand jury indicts Jack Williams, a lobbyist for Tyson Foods, for lying to the FBI and the Agriculture Department during a preliminary probe of Espy in early 1994.
-- Sept. 24, 1996 - Federal grand jury convicts Sun Diamond Growers, a California ag cooperative, of illegally giving Espy nearly $6,000 in gifts.
-- Oct. 16, 1996 - Federal grand jury indicts lobbyist Richard Douglas, a longtime friend of Espy and employee of Sun-Diamond Growers, for giving Espy illegal gifts.
-- Nov. 13, 1996 - Mississippi farmer and Espy friend Brook Keith Mitchell pleads guilty to illegally conspiring to collect more than $700,000 in government farm payments while Espy was secretary.
-- Nov. 19, 1996 - Federal grand jury indicts Norris Faust, a senior Agriculture Department official based in Mississippi, for lying in the Espy probe.

-- Feb. 13, 1997 - Federal grand jury acquits two former executives of Crop Growers Corp. insurance company of making illegal contributions to unsuccessful congressional campaign of Espy's brother, Henry.
-- March 21, 1997 - Federal jury convicts Tyson Foods Inc. lobbyist Jack Williams of two counts of lying during an investigation of Espy.

-- April 22, 1997 - Federal grand jury indicts Espy's former chief of staff Ronald Blackley on charges of lying to investigators to conceal the receipt of $22,000 in consulting fees earned after he joined Espy's staff.
